name: StorePay
why: The direct competitor and the cleanest local site. Headline, two buttons, three numbers and press badges in one calm first screen.
take: Three numbers right under the buttons: 680,000+ users, 9,000+ merchants, 5.3 million purchases
Three phone screens that walk through invoice, split terms and confirmation
Light and dark toggle, plus text-size controls for accessibility
skip: The right half of the hero stayed empty in our capture
The token section (SPCFIN) pulls attention away from the pay-later story

name: Toki
why: Super-app positioning. Opens on a full-screen lifestyle photo, then turns black with one large photo card per product pillar.
take: One card per pillar (Lifestyle, Shop, Pay, Mobile) with real UI chips over photography
Credit limits shown as coloured tiles: 1,000,000₮, 3,000,000₮, 8,000,000₮
Closing band with a phone and all three store badges
skip: Sky-and-person hero is the same idea as Revolut, so it will not feel distinctive
The English slogan tells a new visitor nothing about what the app does

name: Pocket
why: Digital lender. The home page is a rotating campaign banner followed by a loan-terms table next to a phone.
take: Loan terms as a plain table beside the app screen: amount, rate and term at a glance
skip: Rotating banner hero: the message changes before you finish reading it
Long empty stretches further down the page

name: Hipay
why: Payment wallet on a 2019-style template: phone render, icon trio, partner logos, contact form. Useful as the baseline to beat.
take: Merchant onboarding as 01, 02, 03 on a full pink band
Partner logo row
skip: Generic phone mockup with an all-caps slogan
Blog and contact form on the home page make it long and unfocused

name: MonPay
why: Mobicom's wallet. Tidy hero with three store badges (App Store, Google Play, AppGallery) sitting where the button would be.
take: Store badges in the hero, including Huawei AppGallery
Partner count as a section title: 6,000+ partner organisations
skip: All-caps headline with no concrete benefit
Two overlapping phone screenshots too small to read

name: Simple
why: Digital lender. Tilted phone renders and a teal paragraph where the headline should be.
take: Audience split in the nav: citizens, business, merchants, investors
skip: A six-line paragraph as the hero headline
No button or download prompt in the first screen

name: Sono
why: Fintech lender with the most current-looking local layout: centred headline, small pill label, two buttons, stats row, product cards.
take: Pill label above the headline that says what the company is
Four-number stats card overlapping the edge of the hero
Product cards with one-line terms
skip: Large empty purple block in the hero (a video that had not loaded in our capture)

name: BiD today
why: The lender's current site and the older BiD app's home. Opens on a loan calculator with the horse mascot over a city photo.
take: A working calculator in the first screen: move a slider, see the monthly payment
The mascot gives the brand a face that BID Pay could reuse sparingly
skip: Red and navy identity: BID Pay is orange, so the two need a visible link without sharing a palette
Corporate sections (about, news, sustainability) do not belong on a product page

name: Klarna
why: The category leader. Photo carousel hero with a pink Get-the-app QR card, then a pinned section that steps through five promises.
take: QR card fixed to the corner of the hero on desktop
Four headline numbers directly under the hero
Pinned list where one line lights up at a time as you scroll
Real Trustpilot reviews
skip: Carousel hero hides the main message behind rotating campaigns

name: Affirm
why: Pay-over-time lender. Dark navy, thin type with one italic word, and a seasonal headline. The product is explained in stacked glass cards.
take: One italic word in the headline: warmth without illustration
A store search field as its own section
App rating with a QR code beside the footer
skip: Seasonal hero says nothing about how payment works
Low contrast inside the card stack

name: Afterpay
why: Shortest page of the set: fashion photo, a white card with one sentence and a QR code, three benefits, done.
take: Hero card: one line, one sentence, one QR code
Three plain benefits with small icons and no boxes
The offer in three words: Pay in 4
skip: Editorial photography only works with a real shoot

name: Tabby
why: Gulf BNPL turned money app. Mint green first screen, store ratings above the headline, a crowd of drawn characters, QR button.
take: Store ratings above the headline: 4.8 stars with review counts
Each feature gets its own colour tile with a phone screen inside
Closing band repeats the hero colour with a hand-held phone and QR
Wordmark as tall as the footer
skip: The character illustrations are theirs. Copying the style would read as Tabby

name: Tamara
why: Saudi BNPL. Heavy navy headline with a QR under it, and benefit chips floating over a portrait: No late fees, Sharia compliant.
take: Floating chips that state the terms in two words each
Four photo cards in a grid, one promise per card
Product carousel that shows what you can actually buy
FAQ accordion before the footer
skip: Sparkle decorations will date quickly

name: Atome
why: Southeast Asian BNPL. Yellow comic-style campaign hero, then a store directory. The page is mostly a shop window.
take: QR card that follows you down the whole page
Merchant tiles by category right after the hero
A plain sentence: split your purchase into 3 or more payments
skip: A prize-campaign hero is out of date in weeks
Busy: yellow, comic art, photos and tiles all compete

name: Zip
why: US BNPL. Deep purple with a lime button, and the best one-liner in the category: split big payments into not-so-big ones.
take: Headline plus one line that says exactly what the product does
Three store ratings under the button
How it works as a pinned phone that changes while the steps scroll past: anywhere, online, in store
Calendar screen showing that a payment date can be moved
skip: Purple on purple is hard to read in places

name: Cash App
why: The whole home page is one green screen: six words, one phone, two buttons. Nothing else.
take: Total colour commitment: brand green from edge to edge
A real app screen as the only image
Proof that a home page can be one screen long
skip: It works because everyone already knows Cash App. A new product has more explaining to do

name: Revolut
why: A portrait against blue sky with the account balance floating over it. Then cinematic full-width photos, one per product.
take: App UI floating directly over a photo instead of inside a phone frame
One full-screen scene per feature
Plans table at the end
skip: Needs a campaign-grade photo shoot
Toki already uses this look locally

name: Current
why: US neobank. White page, very large light type, one photo, a phone-number field instead of a button, press logos below.
take: Phone-number field in the hero: get the download link by SMS
Press logo row closing the first screen
Collage illustrations that mix photos with drawn shapes
Testimonials with store star ratings
skip: Long legal footer

name: Fluz
why: Cashback app. Dark warm gradient and a condensed all-caps headline, with a Business / Personal switch above it.
take: Audience switch in the hero: the BiD / BID Pay question could use the same control
Short all-caps headline: YOUR MONEY ON MAX
Blunt one-line statement bands between sections
skip: The dark brown palette feels heavy for shopping

name: Jeton
why: Wallet app. Coral-to-peach gradient, a glass disc and huge white type. Orange-family colour used softly rather than loudly.
take: How to make warm orange feel premium: gradient, glass, white type
Store badges in the hero
Single words that fill the screen as you scroll: Add, Send, Exchange
Closing line: 1 million users, plus you
skip: Very long page with one idea per screen
Regulatory pop-up on arrival

name: Uglycash
why: Stablecoin account. Black condensed capitals stacked over a phone, neon tiles, and a wordmark as tall as the footer.
take: Headline as a provocation: YOUR BANK WON'T DO THIS
Three-card how-it-works straight after the hero
A one-sentence statement band with a real number in it
skip: Deliberately rough. Wrong tone for a licensed lender

name: Origin
why: AI financial advisor. Serif headline over a photographed sky, a phone rising from the bottom edge, then near-black sections.
take: Phone cropped by the bottom of the hero so the screen reads large
Award laurels as quiet proof
Nature photography inside cards to warm up a dark page
skip: Serif plus sky reads as wealth management, not shopping

name: Mercury
why: Business banking. A desk on a mountain at dawn, a thin centred headline and an email field. The benchmark for calm.
take: One surreal image that carries the brand promise
Sign-up field in the hero
Slow, restrained scroll motion
skip: Built for founders. Too quiet for a consumer shopping app

name: Ramp
why: Corporate cards. White, one sentence, an email field with a yellow button, and the product working underneath.
take: Five-word headline: Time is money. Save both.
Product UI shown in use under the hero, not as a flat screenshot
Thin announcement strip above the nav
skip: B2B density further down the page

name: Titan
why: Wealth manager. Black, a serif wordmark the width of the page, three lines of plain copy, employer logos.
take: Proof through who uses it: trusted by employees of…
Four facts in a row with no decoration
skip: Formal and exclusive on purpose. The opposite of pay-later

name: Fruitful
why: Financial planning. Soft blue-green wash, centred headline, and a question field with five goal chips under it.
take: Goal chips under the hero: tap what you came for
A phone that stays pinned while the text beside it changes
Award badges directly under the first screen
Customer photos with quotes
skip: A chat-style input promises a conversation the product must then deliver

name: MetaMask
why: Crypto wallet. Condensed black headline, one gradient shape, then a grid of bright illustrated cards.
take: Four colour-blocked cards in a row, each a different product
Orange closing banner with a QR code
Stat strip of three numbers with two-word labels
skip: Crypto cues throughout: tickers, trading screens

name: Slush
why: Crypto wallet. The name fills the screen in black capitals over a 3D blue ribbon, with sticker icons scattered on top.
take: Stickers and 3D objects layered over the type
Rounded page frame: the whole site sits inside a card
Marquee band repeating one call to action
skip: Maximal. Every section shouts

name: Headspace
why: Not finance. It is here as the best-known orange brand on the web: an orange sun, a pink-to-peach wash, blue buttons.
take: Orange as the hero object, not the background
A contrasting button colour, so the action does not vanish into the brand colour
Goal picker right under the hero
Three big numbers over a sky photo
skip: Discount-led hero

name: CRED
why: Indian credit-card rewards club. Pure black, lowercase serif, and a QR code in the first screen. The closest thing to Night Glass that already exists.
take: Download QR card in the corner of a fully dark hero
A paragraph that lights up word by word as you scroll
Neon-lit product tiles on black, one glow colour per feature
Ratings as giant numerals: 4.8 and 4.8
skip: Members-only tone (“not everyone gets it”) is wrong for a product that wants everyone
Low-contrast grey body text on black

name: Robinhood Gold Card
why: One gold card standing in a pool of light, and a thin serif headline. The card is the whole hero.
take: A single 3D card as the hero object: the BiD debit card could play this part
Light that fades from black into a warm glow behind the object
Three plain facts in a row under the fold
Wordmark filling the footer
skip: Serif plus gold says exclusive. BID Pay needs to feel reachable

name: Lunar
why: Danish neobank. Dim evening photo, a glass tablet floating beside the person, three benefits with icons, green button.
take: A glass 3D object layered into a real photograph
Three one-line benefits in the hero instead of a paragraph
Trustpilot and App Store ratings right under the button
Closing band in the brand colour with a QR code
skip: Switches between dark, white and green sections, so the mood breaks

name: Atlas Card
why: Invite-only charge card. A glass card over a fogged city, then full-screen photographs with a single line of small text each.
take: Glass card floating over a city: the Ulaanbaatar skyline could do the same job
Cinematic full-width photos with almost no words
Restraint: one typeface, one size, a lot of black
skip: So quiet it explains nothing about the product
Luxury-only audience

name: Wealthsimple
why: Canadian investing app. Navy hero with a slowly turning gold coin, then one sculpted 3D object per product.
take: One 3D object per feature: coin, card, mountain, pie
Product list set as five very large words
Email field in the hero
Closing proof line: trusted by over 4 million Canadians
skip: Alternates dark and cream sections

name: Apple Card
why: Pastel gradient, a phone rising from the bottom edge, and a grid of tiles where two or three huge words do all the talking.
take: Tiles with one claim each in very large type: No fees. Not even hidden ones.
Gradient as a brand surface instead of a flat colour
The physical card gets its own dark, dramatic tile
skip: Light and pastel: borrow the tile system, not the palette

name: Copilot Money
why: Budgeting app and Apple Design Award finalist. Soft blue wash, a phone cropped by the bottom of the hero, three small proof chips.
take: Three proof chips under the subtitle: award, platforms, 4.8 stars
Phone cropped by the fold so the screen reads large
Each feature in its own softly tinted card with one line of copy
Ratings and reviews before the footer
skip: Light theme: use the structure, not the colour

name: Toss
why: Korea’s finance super-app. A rounded photo that cross-fades as you scroll, then phones on white with one short line each.
take: Hero photo inside a rounded frame, changing while the headline stays put
One sentence per feature: Send money in seconds
Super-app scope explained without a feature grid
skip: Very long, with little variation between sections

name: Slash
why: Business banking. Black, a card set into dark stone, serif headlines with one italic word, and a gold stats row.
take: Photographed 3D card as the hero image
Rating chip above the headline: 4.8 stars
Four gold numbers in a row on black
One italic word per headline to break the seriousness
skip: B2B dashboard screenshots further down

name: Discord
why: Chat app. Indigo night sky, heavy capitals, and features shown in large rounded glass cards.
take: Glass cards with a thick translucent border, alternating left and right
All-caps headlines in a heavy weight, close to what you liked in Uglycash
Closing joke: YOU CAN’T SCROLL ANYMORE. BETTER GO CHAT.
Marquee band of single words
skip: The mascot characters are a brand of their own

name: Framer
why: Website builder, not finance. Included for one thing: product UI framed by a glowing edge on pure black.
take: Glow outline around a UI panel: the Night Glass effect done cleanly
Logo row in white on black
Dense dark product sections that stay readable
skip: Tool-for-professionals density

name: Sezzle
why: US BNPL. Dark violet with a glowing outlined button, three award laurels and three phones fanned across the fold.
take: Glow around the download button itself
Award laurels between the button and the phones
Pinned scenes that swap as you scroll: shop, play, earn
skip: Three-part headline tries to say everything at once
Long pinned sections with little on screen

name: Zilch
why: UK pay-over-time card. Mint ground and green type as tall as the screen, with a 3D ribbon wrapped around a phone.
take: Headline at poster size: three words fill the hero
Legal terms set small but right beside the claim
Grid of green tiles, each a short promise: No late fees. No jargon.
Marquee of the wordmark before the footer
skip: Mint green is theirs
The plans table adds length

name: Podeli
why: Alfa-Bank’s BNPL. A Cyrillic headline that states the offer outright: split the payment into 4 parts. Product photos sit on a pink card.
take: The offer as the headline, in heavy Cyrillic
Four small cards under the hero: nothing extra, the limit, 4 payments, 10,000+ products
Catalogue of what you can buy, right on the home page
Dark app band with a QR code
FAQ accordion
skip: Service-notice banner above the hero

name: Dolyame
why: T-Bank’s BNPL. Pink card hero with a 3D icon and a sharp line: postpone the payment, not the shopping.
take: Headline with a twist instead of a description
Three benefits in one row, icon above, no boxes
How-to-pay stepper beside a phone in a coloured circle
QR code inside a phone frame for the app section
skip: Store and product grids make it feel like a marketplace

name: Yandex Split
why: Yandex’s BNPL in one screen: a green band, the name, one sentence, then where you can use it. Nothing else.
take: One-sentence pitch: split the payment into parts with no overpayment
Partner list as the only content after the hero
Heavy geometric Cyrillic at display size
skip: Too bare to stand alone as BID Pay’s page

name: Kaspi.kz
why: Kazakhstan’s super-app and the regional benchmark for paying in instalments. App icon, name, one line, phone.
take: Hero built from the app icon itself
Claim of rank: super-app No. 1 in Kazakhstan
Products as a horizontal row of plain cards
Large QR code as the final section
skip: Catalogue-style product list with little visual craft

name: Alif
why: Uzbek fintech with instalment shopping. Mint card hero with store badges and a QR code side by side.
take: Store badges and QR together in the hero
Ring of 2,000+ service icons as a proof graphic
QR repeated at the close with ratings
skip: Green on mint is low contrast in places

name: Ard
why: Ard’s super-app. Photo hero, then black sections with a 3D phone, blue glass shards and a card floating on black.
take: A local site already doing dark with 3D objects: phone, shards, card
Card options shown as one white card on black
Photo bands between the dark sections
skip: English WELCOME TO ARD headline says nothing
Promo pop-up covers the page on arrival
Jumps between photo, black and white sections

name: Zeel
why: P2P lending app. Full-screen mountain video, a two-word promise, an outlined button, then black sections with three big numbers.
take: Cinematic nature video as the hero, close to Mercury and Origin
Three numbers on black: 90,000+, 480,000+, 53.5+ billion
Phone photographed on moss: the product in a real scene
skip: Thin outlined button is easy to miss
Short page with little explanation

name: M bank
why: Mongolia’s digital bank. Teal gradient hero with a phone and card, then dark sections. The most polished bank site locally.
take: Gradient hero with a real phone and Visa card
Dark blocks for business features
Download section with a QR tile and store badges
skip: Rotating hero banner
Blog on the home page

name: NetCapital
why: Lender behind NetPay. White page, a pill-shaped headline, and three photo cards for personal, business and savings.
take: Audience cards with real photos: personal, business, savings
Floating quick-links bar at the bottom of the hero
Dark band with a loan-card carousel
skip: Carousel hero
News section on the home page
